whatItIs.text: Tomatoes picked ripe and sealed in tins — usually plum types for sauce work; the canning process makes them a cooked-product from the start, which is why they beat winter fresh tomatoes.

historyNote.text: The tomato reached Eurasia with the Spanish in the 16th century, but Europe treated it first as an ornamental plant, assumed to be poisonous like its nightshade relatives; its name comes from the Nahuatl tomatl.

howToChoose.text: Choose tins without dents, rust, or bulges; whole peeled in juice is the most versatile buy (diced holds firmness, passata skips the work).

storage.text: Tins keep in the cupboard until their date; leftovers decant to a container — never store open tins in the fridge.

useItUp.text: Half a tin becomes shakshuka, butter sauce, or soup — simmer with a pinch of sugar if acidity bites; leftover juice bounces into bloody marys or chilli.

substitutions.ratio: 1 tbsp paste + 3/4 cup water per cup
substitutions.note: concentrated flavour, thinner body; simmer longer
